newsitem.title: USA: CFTC delays decision on controversial CBOT plan.
newsitem.headline: CFTC delays decision on controversial CBOT plan.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Thursday it would extend until June 16 the public comment period for controversial proposed changes in the delivery terms of the Chicago Board of Trade's soybean and corn futures contracts.

In a notice published in the Federal Register, CFTC said it decided to extend the comment period for an additional 60 days to give interested farmers, companies and traders a chance to offer suggestions.
CFTC commissioner Brooksley Born had said a few weeks ago that the agency hoped to move quickly to finalize the CBOT contracts' delivery changes.

Last December, the agency told the CBOT that it must modify the delivery terms of the two contracts, and ordered the exchange to come up with a proposal. On April 15, the CBOT membership approved a set of changes proposed by exchange leaders by a two-to-one margin.

But CBOT's proposal to eliminate Toledo and limit delivery sites to a handful on the northern Illinois River drew more than 250 comments from politicans, grain cooperatives and farmers. Most told the CFTC they opposed the plan because of the potential for price manipulation because of the changes, and urged the agency to consider other options.
